## Registered stub coordinate type (`cylindrical`) {#sec-ch03-cylindrical}

status: draft

### Summary

`CoordinateImpl::create` maps `cylindrical` to `CylindricalImpl`, but its `reset` does nothing and the source file that
would define it is disabled by its suffix (`cylindrical.cpp_`). Its one other override, `face_centroid_shift_zero`,
returns `false` (@sec-ch03-facemoments). No widths, centres, areas or volumes are built. The
type is recorded here so that a reader who meets the name knows it does not work.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** N/A: the name `cylindrical` is accepted and builds a coordinate whose `reset` is empty; no metric and no
defining equation.

**Data.** N/A: no metric buffers are built.

**Placement.** Setup only.

**Activation.** YAML `geometry.type: cylindrical`; off by default.

**Guarantee / limits.** None; the zero-shift flag is `false` and a run has no metric buffers.

**Evidence.** `test_coordinate` checks the flag only (exact, boolean); no test steps a solver on this type
(missing evidence).
:::

Local symbols: none.

### Derivation

Not applicable: there is no implemented metric. The disabled file holds an unfinished vector transform, starting with
`vec_from_cartesian` ({{< code src/coord/cylindrical.cpp_ >}}),
which is not compiled.

| zero-shift flag `false` | {{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CylindricalImpl::face_centroid_shift_zero >}} | `face_centroid_shift_zero` | none |

: Code map of the cylindrical stub. {#tbl-ch03-cylindrical-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-cylindrical-code): `create` returns a `Cylindrical` module for the name
({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::create >}}), whose `reset` is the empty override ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CylindricalImpl >}}).

**How to use it.** `geometry.type: cylindrical` is accepted and builds a block, but its coordinate registers no
buffers: no widths, centres, areas or volumes. Do not select it. Nothing refuses it.
({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CylindricalImpl >}}):

```cpp
  explicit CylindricalImpl(const CoordinateOptions& options_,
                           torch::nn::Module* p = nullptr)
      : CoordinateImpl(options_, p) {
    reset();
  }
  void reset() override {}
```

and reads the flag, and steps nothing. No test runs a solver step on this type (missing evidence).


Constructing a block with this type on a source build of the pin succeeds, and its coordinate module lists no
buffers.[^cyl-build]

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Selecting `cylindrical` leaves the run with no metric buffers.
:::

What a run with this type does was not measured; the statement above is read from the code. The switch combinations
that are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
